| [NOTE-001](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-001.md) v2 | Is the United States Still a Liberal Democracy? | Drezner asks whether the US will still be a liberal constitutional democracy in January 2029. He reviews Polity's downgrades (+10 in 2015 to +5 for 2020, and in February 2025 "at the cusp of autocracy"), the Freedom House fall from 92 to 83 (2014–2021, as quoted from Levitsky & Way) and counter-evidence (continued compliance with court orders; Hickman's "not there yet"). He then concludes that "it is hard to disagree" with Levitsky & Way's forecast of competitive authoritarianism, and expects democracy's "precarity" to be the lasting condition. | Read |
| [NOTE-004](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-004.md) v2 | US v. Google remedies opinion | Remedies opinion after the 2024 §2 liability ruling. The court (Mehta, J.) bars exclusive distribution deals for Search, Chrome, Assistant and the Gemini app, with a one-year exit right on all payment deals. It does not ban payments, and it rejects the Chrome and Android divestitures and choice screens. It orders (i) a one-time snapshot of six Search Index fields per document, (ii) Glue and RankEmbed user-interaction training data "at least twice", capped and privacy-treated, and (iii) five-year search and text-ads syndication on ordinary commercial terms (search capped at 40% of queries in year one). "Qualified Competitors" is rewritten so it can include GenAI firms. The term is six years (five plus one of ramp-up). On GenAI, the court finds that grounded chatbots perform an information-retrieval function similar to general search engines, enough to bring GenAI inside the decree. It also finds that plaintiffs "did not establish that Google's scale advantage in Search translates into a quality advantage in GenAI search-assisted responses" (op. p. 156). For that reason it refuses to order sharing of Gemini training data. | Read |
| [NOTE-012](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-012.md) v2 | Russian Hybrid Warfare | Clark argues from open Russian military writing of 2015–2020, chiefly Military Thought and Army Collection, that Russia treats "hybrid war" as a type of war. In his account it is a strategic-level effort to reorient a target state, in which every action, conventional force included, is subordinate to an information campaign. He concludes that a US strategy centred on deterring great-power conventional war can "technically succeed" while losing. The report ends with 12 recommendations (executive-summary count). | Read |

| [NOTE-019](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-019.md) v2 | Reckless disregard for the truth coming from cops, doctors, and scientists | Gelman argues that scientists (a 3-day study titled "long-term"; the power-pose abstract's "instantly become more powerful"), a paid medical expert (Ludmerer's 2002 "no opinion" on smoking and lung cancer) and DHS spokespeople (Lander "assaulting", Padilla "lunging", ICE's unsourced "413 percent" assaults) share one pattern, which he calls "reckless disregard for the truth". In his account it strengthens a weak case, is carried by journals, courts and media, is accepted as a term of art and goes unpunished. | [NOTE-024](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-024.md) v2 | Rhode Island Hospital subpoena order | Judge McElroy quashed DOJ HIPAA administrative subpoena No. 25-1431-032 (18 U.S.C. § 3486) to Rhode Island Hospital on three independent grounds: 1. no congressionally authorized purpose, because DOJ's FDCA off-label "misbranding" theory against a prescribing hospital is not legally cognizable (Facteau; 21 U.S.C. §§ 396, 353(b)(2)); 2. issuance for an improper purpose in bad faith; 3. a Fourteenth Amendment informational-privacy violation for the children, with relief extended to all minors because a DCYF-only carve-out would itself expose DCYF wards. The court enjoined DOJ with respect to patient-identifying information and PHI produced under the subpoena, and stated that it quashed the subpoena, "not the enforcement order entered by the Texas court". An amended order the next day (ECF 44) added "seeking" to the injunction. DOJ appealed (1st Cir. No. 26-1568; argument calendared for Oct 7, 2026). | Read |
